subtitle: Silver Tankgas and the Promise of a Mountain Kingdom

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle close-up on a freshly struck silver coin held against a backdrop of snowy Himalaya and Leh's mud-brick roofs
panels.action: Namgyal Mint Artisan holds up a gleaming silver tankga between thumb and finger, his weathered face half in shadow, the fortress-palace of Leh and distant caravan lines faint behind him in the high, thin air.

dialogue.text: Between barter and foreign rupees, Ladakh forged its own silver voice: the tankga of the Namgyals.

i18n.hi: लेन-देन और परदेसियों के रुपये के बीच, लद्दाख ने अपनी चाँदी की आवाज गढ़ी – नमग्यालों का तंगका।

panels.shot: vast bird’s-eye view over Leh bazaar and the routes snaking towards Kashmir, Tibet and Central Asia
panels.action: An aerial view of Leh bazaar shows tightly packed stalls, yak caravans dusting the road, and distant passes leading west towards Kashmir, east towards Tibet, and north towards Central Asia under a hard blue sky.

dialogue.text: In the seventeenth century, Leh stood at a crossroads of worlds: Kashmir and India to the west, Tibet to the east, Yarkand and Central Asia to the north.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं सदी में लेह दुनिया के मोड़ पर खड़ा था: पश्चिम में कश्मीर-हिंदुस्तान, पूरब में तिब्बत, उत्तर में यारकंद और मध्य एशिया।

panels.shot: mid-shot of a crowded market scene focused on hands exchanging different media of payment
panels.action: In the bustle of the Leh market, a Kashmiri trader weighs Mughal rupees, a Tibetan merchant fingers square-sleeved tangkas, while a local herder offers butter and wool, their hands overlapping over grain measures and metal scales.

dialogue.text: Here, grain and butter paid for labour, Tibetan tangkas followed caravans, Mughal rupees rattled in money-changers’ bowls, and credit travelled on the caravan-master’s word.

i18n.hi: यहाँ मज़दूरी का हक़ अनाज और घी से चुकता होता, कारवाँ के साथ तिब्बती तांका चलते, साहूकारों के कटोरों में मुग़ल रुपये छनकते, और उधार सिर्फ़ कारवाँ सालार की ज़ुबान पर भरोसा था।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot in a dim storehouse, focused on the artisan examining foreign coins under lamplight
panels.action: By lamplight inside a mud-walled storehouse, Namgyal Mint Artisan sits cross-legged, spreading out worn Mughal rupees and Tibetan tangkas on a low table, his brow furrowed as he studies their designs and edges.

dialogue.text: The Namgyal court watched this mixed money with care, weighing foreign silver and copper, and asking a sharp question: whose face, whose promise, ruled these hills?

i18n.hi: नमग्याल दरबार इस मिली‑जुली रक़म पर नज़र रखता, पराई चाँदी‑ताँबा तोलता, और टेढ़ा सवाल करता: किसका चेहरा, किसका वादा, इन पहाड़ों पर हुकूमत करता है?

panels.shot: close-up on the artisan’s hands testing a coin’s weight on a small balance scale
panels.action: A tight focus on Namgyal Mint Artisan’s hands shows him placing a slender Tibetan tangka on one side of a tiny balance scale, matching it with cut silver pieces on the other, his fingers steady and practiced.

dialogue.text: Alexander Cunningham later noted this tangle of currencies around Leh, yet in that tangle the Namgyals began to carve a place for their own coin.

i18n.hi: अलेक्ज़ेंडर कनिंघम ने बाद में लेह के इस करेंसी के घुचपच को लिखा, पर इसी उलझन में नमग्यालों ने अपने सिक्के की जगह बनानी शुरू की।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of the royal mint, with artisans at work amid tools and furnaces
panels.action: Inside a simple but ordered mint near Leh, Namgyal Mint Artisan oversees a few men stoking a clay furnace, others hammering metal strips, and a boy grinding charcoal, all under rafters darkened by smoke.

dialogue.text: A modest royal mint grew by the palace, its walls plain, its fire fierce. From here came the Ladakhi tankga, silver and copper, struck under the Namgyals.

i18n.hi: महल के पास एक सादा शाही टकसाल उगा, दीवारें साधारण, आग जुनूनी। यहीं से निकले लद्दाखी तंगका – चाँदी और ताँबा, नमग्यालों की मुहर के साथ।

panels.shot: close-up on a die being engraved with Buddhist symbols and Tibetan script
panels.action: Namgyal Mint Artisan bends over a metal die, tools in hand, patiently carving a wheel-like Buddhist emblem and curling Tibetan letters into the steel, his breath clouding faintly in the cold air.

dialogue.text: Nicholas Rhodes traced these coins: Buddhist symbols, Tibetan legends, Ladakhi titles. Each tankga carried both the Dharma and the king’s name across the plateau.

i18n.hi: निकोलस रोड्स ने इन सिक्कों के निशान जोड़े: बौद्ध चिह्न, तिब्बती लेख, लद्दाखी ख़िताब। हर तंगका धर्म और राजा दोनों का नाम पठार भर में ढोता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of artisan presenting sample coins to a robed court official in a simple audience hall
panels.action: In a whitewashed audience room, Namgyal Mint Artisan kneels and lays a neat row of new silver and copper pieces on a rug before a robed official, who leans forward, inspecting their shine and clarity.

dialogue.speaker: Namgyal Mint Artisan
dialogue.text: My lord, this tankga bears Ladakh’s weight. Its measure holds steady.

i18n.hi: महाराज, ये तंगका पूरे लद्दाख का भार उठाए है। इसकी तोल डगमग नहीं होती।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind a tax-collector weighing coins at a market stall
panels.action: Seen from behind a tax-collector’s shoulder, a small pile of fresh Ladakhi tankgas lies beside older foreign coins on his portable scales, while Namgyal Mint Artisan watches from the crowd, expression intent.

dialogue.text: These coins did not reach every field or hamlet. Cunningham found that grain and butter still paid most dues, and silver mattered most where the king’s revenue met the trader’s purse.

i18n.hi: ये सिक्के हर खेत‑खलिहान तक न पहुँचे। कनिंघम ने पाया कि ज़्यादातर लगान अभी भी अनाज और घी में चुकता होता, और चाँदी वहीँ गिनी जाती जहाँ राजा की आय व्यापारी की थैली से मिलती।

panels.shot: wide shot of a caravan halt with merchants exchanging different coins before a journey
panels.action: At a windy caravan halt beyond Leh, merchants huddle on the ground, spreading Mughal rupees, Tibetan tangkas, and Ladakhi tankgas on cloths as they bargain over rates, while yaks rest behind them under fluttering prayer flags.

dialogue.text: On the long roads to Lhasa, Srinagar and Yarkand, money-changers juggled three worlds: Indian rupees, Tibetan tangkas, and Ladakh’s own pieces, each with its weight and trust.

i18n.hi: ल्हासा, श्रीनगर और यारकंद की लंबी सड़कों पर साहूकार तीन दुनिया सँभालते: हिंदुस्तानी रुपये, तिब्बती तांका और लद्दाख के अपने सिक्के – हर एक की अलग तोल, अलग भरोसा।

panels.shot: mid-shot of the artisan listening to a Central Asian trader comparing coins
panels.action: Namgyal Mint Artisan stands near a tent as a fur-hatted Central Asian trader holds up a Ladakhi tankga beside a Persianate coin, speaking animatedly while pointing to their rims and scripts.

dialogue.text: Central Asian and Persianate styles brushed this frontier; foreign coins brought new scripts and forms. Yet Ladakh’s mint kept its own mix of Tibetan letters and Buddhist signs.

i18n.hi: मध्य एशिया और फ़ारसी दुनिया की रंगत इस सरहद से भी टकराई; पराये सिक्के नई लिपियाँ और ढाँचे लाए। फिर भी लद्दाख की टकसाल ने अपना तिब्बती अक्षर और बौद्ध निशान नहीं छोड़ा।

panels.shot: close-up on a table showing successive issues of Ladakhi coins laid in chronological order
panels.action: On a low wooden table, Namgyal Mint Artisan arranges different Ladakhi coins in a careful line: early crude strikes, later clearer legends, varying sizes and symbols, his finger moving from one to the next.

dialogue.text: Across two centuries the tankga shifted: thicker or thinner, sharper or blurred, legends changing with rulers, yet always announcing that Ladakh was not just a road, but a kingdom.

i18n.hi: दो सदियों में तंगका बदलता रहा: कभी मोटा, कभी पतला, कभी धार तेज़, कभी धुँधली; हुक्मरान बदले तो लिखावट भी, लेकिन हर बार ये जताता रहा कि लद्दाख सिर्फ़ राह नहीं, पूरा राज्य है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a peasant family paying tax partly in grain, partly with a single coin
panels.action: In a village storehouse, a tax-collector notes piles of grain while a herder’s family places a single worn tankga on a tray, Namgyal Mint Artisan nearby, quietly observing the mix of harvest and silver.

dialogue.text: Most households still met the king with sacks of barley and butter. A single coin might stand beside a year’s grain, a small glint of metal amid the weight of harvest.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादातर घर आज भी राजा से भूसे की बोरियाँ और घी के मटके लेकर मिलते। एक अकेला सिक्का साल भर की फ़सल के ढेर के साथ बस हल्की‑सी धातु की चमक था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Leh palace and town, with a subtle overlay of drifting coin images in the sky
panels.action: The Leh palace rises above the clustered town under a clear sky, while faint, ghostly images of Ladakhi tankgas seem to drift above the rooftops, as if memories of promises once struck in silver.

dialogue.text: Modern catalogues still struggle to list every issue. Museum trays in distant cities hold scattered pieces of this story, each coin a clue to how Ladakh saw itself and spoke to the world.

i18n.hi: आज के कैटलॉग भी हर इश्यू गिन नहीं पाते। दूर शहरों के म्यूज़ियम की ट्रे में इस कहानी के बिखरे टुकड़े पड़े हैं – हर सिक्का एक सुराग कि लद्दाख ने खुद को कैसे देखा, और दुनिया से कैसे बात की।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the artisan’s face, older now, reflecting on a coin turning between his fingers
panels.action: Older now, with deeper lines around his eyes, Namgyal Mint Artisan sits alone, turning a tarnished silver tankga slowly between his fingers, his gaze distant and thoughtful in the fading evening light.

dialogue.speaker: Namgyal Mint Artisan
dialogue.text: Metal fades, but the promise it carried stays in men’s minds.

i18n.hi: धातु घिस जाती है, पर उसमें छुपा वादा लोगों की याद में रह जाता है।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of a Ladakhi tankga resting beside a modern coin on a neutral surface
panels.action: On a plain surface, a Ladakhi silver tankga rests beside a modern coin, their different scripts and symbols stark, while Namgyal Mint Artisan’s hand hovers just above, as if connecting past and present.

dialogue.text: A coin is a kingdom’s promise made visible; in the thin air of Ladakh, the Namgyal tankga turned that promise into silver that crossed passes, markets and centuries.

i18n.hi: सिक्का एक राज्य का दिखता हुआ वादा है; लद्दाख की पतली हवा में नमग्याल तंगका ने उस वादे को ऐसी चाँदी बनाया जो दर्रों, बाज़ारों और सदियों को पार कर गई।

title_i18n.hi: चाँदी के तंगका, लद्दाख की ज़ुबान

subtitle_i18n.en: Silver Tankgas and the Promise of a Mountain Kingdom
subtitle_i18n.hi: चाँदी के तंगका और पहाड़ी राज्य का वादा
